text: On the road it is allowed to:

options.a: Pick up or drop off passengers or cargo anywhere
options.b: Leave animals loose or place them so that they block traffic only a little
options.c: Pick up or drop off passengers in authorized places.
options.d: Carry out street trading, mobile or stationary

gist: Where you may drop off passengers
explanation: Passengers may be picked up or dropped off only in authorized places. The other options are all violations. Anywhere is not allowed; animals and street trading on the road are banned.
trap: Option a also mentions passengers, but «en cualquier lugar» (anywhere) is a violation. Look for «lugares autorizados» (authorized places).

c.tr: Pick up or drop off passengers

text: Regarding traffic control or regulation devices (signs, lights, markings):

options.a: Only pedestrians are required to obey them
options.b: Drivers and pedestrians are required to obey them, except when an instruction from the National Police of Peru assigned to traffic indicates otherwise
options.c: Only drivers are required to obey them.
options.d: Drivers are required to obey them, even when the National Police of Peru assigned to traffic may indicate otherwise.

gist: Who must obey traffic control devices
explanation: Everyone must obey signs, lights and markings: drivers and pedestrians alike. But a traffic police officer's instruction overrides any device. So the right answer is the one with «salvo» (except).
trap: Option d looks similar, but «aun cuando» (even when) means obeying the device even against the officer. That is wrong. Look for «salvo» (except) and «conductores y peatones» (drivers and pedestrians).

b.es: de la Policía Nacional del Perú
b.tr: from the National Police of Peru

text: The regulatory vertical sign R-6 «no left turn» means that:

options.a: Turning left is prohibited, and therefore the U-turn is also prohibited.
options.b: Turning left is prohibited; however, the U-turn is allowed.
options.c: The only direction of travel is straight ahead.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: A U-turn is basically a double left turn. So where left turns are banned, U-turns are banned too. Option b says the opposite, so it is wrong.
trap: Options a and b start the same. The difference is at the end: «también está prohibido» (also prohibited) is right; «está permitido el giro en U» (U-turn allowed) is wrong.

a.es: Está prohibido voltear a la izquierda
a.tr: It is prohibited to turn left

a.es: está prohibido el giro en U.

b.es: Está prohibido voltear a la izquierda,
b.tr: It is prohibited to turn left,

b.es: está permitido el giro en U.

text: The regulatory vertical sign R-3 means that:

options.a: We are approaching an area where traffic is restricted.
options.b: Overtaking vehicles is allowed.
options.c: The only direction of travel is straight ahead.
options.d: None of the options is correct

explanation: R-3 is a blue circle with a white arrow pointing up. It is a mandatory direction sign: go straight only. Turning left or right is not allowed here.
trap: A blue circle means an obligation, not a prohibition. Key words: «continuar de frente» (go straight ahead).

text: On roads, a broken yellow centre line on the pavement means that:

options.a: It is allowed to cross into the other lane to overtake, if it is safe to do so.
options.b: It is not allowed to cross into the other lane to overtake.
options.c: The carriageway of the road you are driving on is narrowing.
options.d: You are at a pedestrian crossing.

explanation: A yellow line separates opposite directions of traffic. A broken line may be crossed. So overtaking across it is allowed, but only when it is safe. A solid yellow line must not be crossed.
trap: Options a and b differ by one word: «No está permitido» (not allowed) applies to a solid line. For a broken line the right one is «Está permitido… si es seguro» (allowed if safe).

text.tr: that are of the central type

a.es: si es que es seguro hacerlo.
a.tr: if it is safe to do so.

b.tr: It is not allowed to cross

c.es: de la vía por donde se circula.
c.tr: of the road being driven on.

text: The amber or yellow light of a traffic signal means that:

options.a: Vehicles must proceed.
options.b: Vehicles must stop.
options.c: Vehicles must speed up.
options.d: Vehicles must stop before entering the intersection if their speed and position allow it; otherwise, they must cross and clear the intersection.

explanation: Amber is a warning: red is coming next. If you can stop safely before the intersection, stop. If it is too late to brake, cross and clear the intersection. Speeding up on amber is not allowed.
trap: Option b «deben detenerse» (must stop) is incomplete. The right answer is the long one with the condition «si su velocidad y ubicación lo permiten» (if speed and position allow).

d.es: antes de ingresar a la intersección

text: The traffic light colours mean the following: red: _____; amber or yellow: _____; green: ____.

options.a: Stop - caution - go.
options.b: Stop - go with caution - fast traffic.
options.c: Slow down - caution - go fast.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: Meaning of red, amber and green
explanation: Red means stop (detención). Amber means caution, get ready to stop (prevención). Green means go (paso). No colour ever means «drive fast».
trap: Options b and c contain «rápida/rápido» (fast), which is always wrong. The right sequence is «Detención - prevención - paso».

text: What does a green arrow on a vehicle traffic light indicate?

options.a: You may continue with caution only in the direction of the arrow and from the lane that this arrow controls.
options.b: Driving in the direction shown by the arrow is not allowed.
options.c: Only the round light must be obeyed.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: Green arrow on a traffic light
explanation: A green arrow allows you to go only where it points. And only from the lane it controls. Drive with caution: there may be pedestrians.
trap: Option b says «No está permitida» (not allowed); it is the opposite: a green arrow allows. Look for «dirección de la flecha» (direction of the arrow) and «carril» (lane).

a.es: en la dirección de la flecha
a.tr: in the direction of the arrow

b.es: en el sentido que indica la flecha.
b.tr: in the direction the arrow shows.

text: The following regulatory vertical sign R-53:

options.a: Prohibits parking.
options.b: Prohibits the driver from stopping the vehicle inside the intersection area.
options.c: Prohibits loading and unloading.
options.d: Prohibits the movement of motor vehicles

explanation: R-53 means «do not stop inside the intersection». Do not enter the intersection if there is no room beyond it. Otherwise you block the traffic. It is about stopping in the intersection, not about parking.
trap: All options start with «Prohíbe» (prohibits). Look for «intersección» (intersection) and «detener» (to stop).

b.es: dentro del área de la intersección.

text: You reach an intersection and see the traffic light with a red left arrow and the round green light on at the same time. The correct action is:

options.a: Go in any direction, since the round light is green.
options.b: Go, but the left turn is prohibited by the red arrow.
options.c: Go only to the left, since going straight is prohibited.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: Red left arrow with green light
explanation: The round green light allows going straight and turning right. The red arrow bans only the left turn. So: go, but do not turn left.
trap: Option c reverses it: «únicamente hacia la izquierda» (only to the left). The truth is the opposite: «giro a la izquierda está prohibido» (left turn prohibited).

text: You reach an intersection where the traffic light shows a flashing light. Which statement is correct:

options.a: If the flashing light is red, it is equivalent to a «YIELD» sign
options.b: If the flashing light is amber, you have priority, but must slow down and continue with caution.
options.c: If the flashing light is green, it is equivalent to a “STOP” sign.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: Flashing red equals a «PARE» (stop) sign: stop, then go. Flashing amber means you have priority, but slow down and be careful. A flashing green is never a stop sign.
trap: Option a is a mix-up: flashing red means «PARE» (stop), not «CEDA EL PASO» (yield). Look for «ámbar» (amber) and «precaución» (caution).

a.es: Si la luz intermitente es roja,
a.tr: If the flashing light is red,

b.es: Si la luz intermitente es ámbar,
b.tr: If the flashing light is amber,

c.es: Si la luz intermitente es verde,
c.tr: If the flashing light is green,

text: Is a flashing red light the same as a STOP (PARE) sign?

options.a: True.
options.b: It is true only as long as a traffic police officer is also there signalling stop.
options.c: False
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: Yes, it is true. A flashing red works like a PARE sign: full stop, then go when clear. No police officer is needed for this.
trap: Option b also starts with «verdad» (true) but adds the condition «siempre y cuando… Policía» (only if a police officer is there). The condition is false; it is a trap. The right answer is the short «Verdad.»

text: When approaching an intersection where a left turn is allowed, the correct behaviour is:

options.a: Turn from any lane.
options.b: Move into the right lane, then turn with caution.
options.c: Move into the lane with the least traffic, then turn with caution.
options.d: Signal the left turn with the indicators, position the vehicle in advance in the left lane and turn with caution.

explanation: A left turn is made from the left lane. First switch on the left indicator, then move into the left lane in advance. Then turn with caution. The right lane or the «emptiest» lane is wrong.
trap: Three options end with «girar con precaución» (turn with caution). The right one has «luces direccionales» (indicators) and «carril… de la izquierda» (left lane).

text.es: con giro permitido a la izquierda,

d.es: Hacer la señal de volteo a la izquierda
en el carril de circulación de la izquierda

text: When changing lanes on a one-way road with multiple lanes, what is the correct behaviour?

options.a: Switch on the indicators first, look for a gap and change lanes with caution.
options.b: Find a gap, then change lanes with caution; indicators are not necessary for lane changes.
options.c: Warn by using the horn, identify a gap and change lanes with caution.
options.d: Changing lanes on one-way roads is prohibited.

explanation: The order is simple: indicator first, then find a gap, then change lanes carefully. The indicator is always mandatory. The horn is not used for this.
trap: Option b also mentions «luces direccionales», but with «no es necesario» (not necessary), which is wrong. Look for «encender las luces direccionales primero» (switch on the indicators first).

text.es: en una vía de un solo sentido

a.es: Se deben encender las luces direccionales
a.tr: The indicators must be switched on

a.es: y realizar el cambio de carril

b.es: luego cambiar de carril con precaución;

c.es: y realizar el cambio de carril

d.es: en vías de un solo sentido.

text: Regarding level crossings with railway tracks, choose the correct statement:

options.a: Vehicles travelling on the railway have right of way over those travelling on the road that crosses it.
options.b: Vehicles on the road that crosses the railway line have right of way over those on the railway.
options.c: The vehicle that arrives first has priority.
options.d: The driver coming from the right of the other has priority.

gist: Right of way at railway crossings
explanation: The train always has right of way. It cannot stop quickly or swerve. Cars at the crossing must yield.
trap: Options a and b sound almost the same, with the words swapped. Correct: «por la vía férrea tienen preferencia» (those on the railway have priority).

text.es: Respecto a los cruces a nivel

a.es: por la vía férrea tienen preferencia
por la vía que la cruza.
a.tr: on the road that crosses it.

b.es: por la vía que cruza la línea férrea
b.tr: on the road that crosses the railway line

d.es: que viene por la derecha del otro.
d.tr: who comes from the right of the other.

text: The traffic light is red, but the National Police officer controlling traffic signals to continue. You should:

options.a: Stop until it changes to green.
options.b: Continue driving.
options.c: Be alert.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: Red light versus police officer's signal
explanation: The officer's signal outranks the traffic light. If the officer signals «go», you go, even on red. The order of priority: police officer, then traffic light, then signs.
trap: Look for «Continuar la marcha» (continue driving). «Detenerse» (stop) is the trap for those who only look at the light.

text.es: Ante la señal de color rojo
y la indicación de continuar la marcha
del efectivo de la Policía Nacional del Perú

a.es: hasta que cambie a luz verde.

text: It is prohibited to park a vehicle:

options.a: On curves.
options.b: Inside an intersection.
options.c: In front of the entrance to garages and military or police premises.
options.d: All of the options are correct.

explanation: All three places listed are no-parking places. A curve: you cannot be seen. An intersection: you block traffic. A garage or military entrance: you block access.
trap: Each of a, b and c is true on its own. When all are true, choose «Todas las alternativas son correctas» (all options are correct).

c.es: y de recintos militares o policiales.

text: The following regulatory vertical sign (R-29):

options.a: Prohibits the use of the horn on urban roads.
options.b: Prohibits the use of the horn on highways.
options.c: Prohibits the use of the horn.
options.d: Prohibits making noise.

explanation: R-29 shows a crossed-out horn in a red circle. It means: using the horn is prohibited. No conditions: neither urban roads nor highways are mentioned. It is only about the horn, not any noise.
trap: Options a and b add a place: «en vías urbanas» (urban roads), «en carreteras» (highways). The sign specifies nothing. The right one is the shortest: «Prohíbe el uso de la bocina.»

a.es: Prohíbe el uso de la bocina
a.tr: Prohibits the use of the horn

b.es: Prohíbe el uso de la bocina
b.tr: Prohibits the use of the horn

c.es: Prohíbe el uso de la bocina.
c.tr: Prohibits the use of the horn.

text: A fine will be imposed, and the licence cannot be obtained for 3 years, on a person who:

options.a: Drives a motor vehicle without having a driving licence.
options.b: Drives a vehicle that lacks the equipment to provide maximum comfort to its occupants.
options.c: Drives a vehicle without SOAT.
options.d: a and c are correct

explanation: Driving without a licence is a very serious offence (M.1). It brings a fine and a 3-year ban on getting a licence. Driving without SOAT is also an offence, but with no 3-year ban. So «a y c» is wrong.
trap: Option d «a y c son correctas» (a and c are correct) is tempting. But SOAT carries no 3-year ban. Look for «sin tener licencia de conducir» (without a licence).

b.es: que no cuente con el equipamiento

text: Suppose you are driving and a vehicle that intends to pass or overtake you catches up with you. What should you do?

options.a: You must increase speed so the other vehicle cannot pass you.
options.b: You must not increase speed until the vehicle has passed you.
options.c: You must drastically reduce your vehicle's speed.
options.d: You must stop your vehicle.

gist: What to do when being overtaken
explanation: When being overtaken, do not get in the way. Do not speed up until the overtaking is complete. Braking hard or stopping is not needed either; it is dangerous.
trap: Options a and b differ by one «No»: «Debe aumentar» (must speed up) is wrong; «No debe aumentar» (must not speed up) is right.

text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.a: The driver must respect the established maximum and minimum speed limits.
options.b: The driver must respect only the maximum speed limits, because there are no minimum limits.
options.c: The driver may drive at any speed he wishes, as long as he does so prudently.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: Peru has both maximum and minimum speed limits. Driving too slowly is also dangerous. The driver must respect both.
trap: Option b claims «no existen límites mínimos» (there are no minimum limits), which is false. Look for «máximos y mínimos» (maximum and minimum).

b.tr: since there are no minimum limits.

c.tr: as long as he does so

text: Which lights must a driver use on urban public roads at night?

options.a: Low beam.
options.b: High beam.
options.c: High beam at intersections and low beam on avenues.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: Which headlights at night in town
explanation: In town at night use low beam only. High beam dazzles other drivers and pedestrians. High beam is for roads outside town with no lighting and no oncoming traffic.
trap: «Bajas» means low beam, «Altas» means high beam. Do not mix them up. Option c with «altas en las intersecciones» (high beam at intersections) is wrong.

text.tr: Which lights must be used by

text: In case of accidents, SOAT covers the injuries suffered by:

options.a: Only the occupants of the vehicle.
options.b: The occupants and third parties who are not occupants of the vehicle.
options.c: Only affected third parties.
options.d: Only the driver of the vehicle.

explanation: SOAT covers everyone injured in the accident. That means people inside the vehicle and outside it: pedestrians, other drivers. Any option with «solo» (only) is wrong.
trap: Three options start with «Solo» (only), which narrows the coverage. The right one has «ocupantes y terceros» (occupants and third parties).

text: Which of the following insurances is required to drive a motor vehicle?

options.a: Any type of personal accident insurance sold by insurance companies.
options.b: Any type of vehicle insurance, provided it covers the occupants and third parties affected by a traffic accident.
options.c: The Compulsory Traffic Accident Insurance - SOAT.
options.d: It is not mandatory to have insurance.

explanation: Only SOAT is mandatory, the compulsory traffic accident insurance. You may not drive without it. Other policies are optional and do not replace SOAT.
trap: Option b describes similar coverage, but «cualquier tipo de seguro vehicular» (any vehicle insurance) is wrong. Look for «SOAT».

text: When is it mandatory to give way to an emergency vehicle or an official vehicle:

options.a: When it emits visible signals.
options.b: When it emits audible signals.
options.c: When it emits audible and visible signals.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: When to yield to emergency vehicles
explanation: You must give way when both the siren and the flashing lights are on. One signal alone is not enough under the rules. Key: «audibles y visibles», both sound and light.
trap: Options a and b name only one kind of signal. The right one has the word «y» (and): «audibles y visibles».

text: If, in the lane you are driving in, you approach a school transport vehicle that is stopped, picking up or dropping off schoolchildren, what must you do?

options.a: Stop the vehicle and not continue driving until the schoolchildren have finished boarding or alighting.
options.b: Overtake on the left side, but with caution.
options.c: Sound the horn to warn that you are passing.
options.d: Overtake very slowly.

gist: Stopped school bus: what to do
explanation: Children may run onto the road at any moment. So you must stop completely and wait. You may drive on only after boarding or alighting is over. Overtaking or honking is not allowed.
trap: Options b and d say «adelantar» (overtake), carefully or slowly. That is the trap: no overtaking at all, only «detener» (stop).

text.tr: picking up or dropping off schoolchildren,

text: What does a red safety triangle placed on the roadway mean?

options.a: The presence of a vehicle immobilised on the public road for some reason.
options.b: A works zone for roadway repair.
options.c: That the vehicle facing it must stop.
options.d: a and c are correct.

gist: Red triangle on the road: meaning
explanation: The triangle is placed behind a broken-down or stopped vehicle. It warns: a vehicle is standing ahead. You do not have to stop, just slow down and pass. So c and d are wrong.
trap: Option d «a y c son correctas» (a and c are correct) is tempting. But c is wrong: «debe detenerse» (must stop) is not a rule.

c.es: Que el vehículo que lo enfrenta

text: The following vertical regulatory sign P-22C indicates that:

options.a: Overtaking is permitted.
options.b: An additional lane is approaching.
options.c: Changing lane is permitted.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: Sign P-22C warns that an extra lane will appear ahead. It is a warning sign, not a permission. It does not say you may overtake or change lane.
trap: Options a and c start with «está permitido» (it is permitted). The sign permits nothing; it only warns: «se aproxima» (approaching) a lane.

text: The vehicle's emergency flashing lights must be used compulsorily:

options.a: To turn at intersections and to warn of lane changes.
options.b: To indicate stopping, standing or parking in a dangerous area, or performing risky manoeuvres.
options.c: During all driving of the vehicle.
options.d: At every intersection.

explanation: Hazard lights are for a vehicle stopped in a dangerous place. Or for a risky manoeuvre. Turns and lane changes use the indicators, not the hazard lights.
trap: Option a is about turns and lane changes. That is the job of «luces direccionales» (indicators), not hazard lights. Look for «zona peligrosa» (dangerous area).

text: At intersections with no Stop or Give Way signs and no traffic light, do two-way roads have right of way over one-way roads of the same classification?

options.a: No.
options.b: Yes.
options.c: It depends on the intersection.
options.d: It is not regulated in the regulations.

explanation: Yes. With no signs or lights, the two-way road has priority. The one-way road of the same class gives way. The rules state this directly.
trap: The answer is the short «Si» (yes). Do not confuse it with «No» (no) and «No se encuentra regulado» (not regulated); both are wrong.

text.es: Pare, Ceda el Paso o Semáforo,
text.tr: Stop, Give Way or a traffic light,

text.es: respecto a las vías de un solo sentido

text: If you approach a STOP (PARE) sign placed vertically or painted on the road, the correct action is:

options.a: Reduce your speed and give way to the vehicles travelling on the cross road.
options.b: Reduce your speed and pass carefully.
options.c: Slow almost to a stop and pass quickly.
options.d: Stop completely, give way to the users who have priority, and then continue with caution.

gist: What to do at a PARE sign
explanation: PARE means stop: you must stop completely. Then give way to those who have priority. Only after that drive on. Just slowing down is not enough.
trap: Options a and b say «disminuir su velocidad» (reduce speed). That is not enough: you must «parar por completo» (stop completely).

d.es: ceder el paso a los usuarios

text: What is the difference between signs P-2A and P-1A?

options.a: There is no difference, they are used interchangeably.
options.b: Sign P-2A is used in situations of greater risk.
options.c: Sign P-1A warns of a sharp curve to the right, while P-2A warns of a gentle curve to the right.
options.d: Sign P-2A warns of a sharp curve to the right, while P-1A warns of a gentle curve to the right.

gist: Difference between signs P-1A and P-2A
explanation: P-1A is a sharp curve to the right (curva pronunciada). P-2A is a gentle curve to the right (curva suave). Remember: lower number, sharper curve.
trap: Options c and d use the same words in a different order. The right one starts with «P-1A … pronunciada» (sharp): that is option c.

text: What does sign R-30F indicate?

options.a: Be careful with slow vehicles.
options.b: Regulates the maximum speed permitted on curves.
options.c: Regulates the maximum speed in rural areas.
options.d: It is not regulated in the regulations.

explanation: The R-30 series are maximum speed signs. R-30F stands before a curve. It tells you the speed allowed through the curve.
trap: Options b and c start the same way. Look for the word «curvas» (curves), not «zonas rurales» (rural areas).

text: What signal must the driver use to reduce speed or stop the vehicle while moving?

options.a: Turn indicators.
options.b: Only the left forearm and hand extended downward outside the vehicle.
options.c: Flashing lights and, in case of force majeure, the left forearm and hand extended downward outside the vehicle, at a right angle to the arm.
options.d: Low beam lights.

explanation: The main signal is the flashing lights (luces intermitentes). The arm is only a backup if the lights fail. Left arm down, at a right angle. Indicators and low beams are not for this.
trap: Option b is also about the arm down, but starts with «solo» (only). The answer is c: lights first, the arm only «en caso de fuerza mayor» (in case of force majeure).

b.es: Solo el antebrazo izquierdo y mano
b.tr: Only the left forearm and hand

c.es: y, en caso de fuerza mayor,
c.tr: and, in case of force majeure,

c.es: utilizar el antebrazo izquierdo y mano
c.tr: use the left forearm and hand

c.es: haciendo ángulo recto con el brazo.
c.tr: at a right angle to the arm.

text: If two vehicles approach an unregulated intersection (no signs) simultaneously from different roads, who has right of way?

options.a: Either of the two.
options.b: The one approaching from the right of the other.
options.c: The one approaching from the left of the other.
options.d: The one who sounds the horn first.

gist: Who goes first with no signs
explanation: The rule is: priority to the right. The vehicle on your right has priority. You give way to it. Sounding the horn gives no priority.
trap: Options b and c differ by one word: «derecha» (right) is correct, «izquierda» (left) is not.

b.tr: from the right of the other.

c.tr: from the left of the other.

text: At an unregulated intersection (no signs), right of way belongs to:

options.a: The vehicle that entered the intersection first.
options.b: The vehicle that sounds the horn first.
options.c: The vehicle that flashes its lights first.
options.d: Any vehicle.

gist: Who goes first at unregulated intersection
explanation: Whoever entered the intersection first goes first. Horn and flashing lights give no priority. It is not a signalling race.
trap: Every option has «primero» (first). Only the one with «ingresó» (entered) is right: entered first, not honked first.

text: At a roundabout, right of way belongs to the vehicle that:

options.a: Wants to enter the roundabout.
options.b: Is already travelling on it.
options.c: Accelerates first.
options.d: Sounds the horn.

gist: Who has priority at a roundabout
explanation: The vehicle already on the roundabout has priority. The one entering gives way. Speed and horn change nothing.
trap: Option a «quiere ingresar» (wants to enter) is the one who gives way. Priority goes to «circula por ella» (travelling on it).

text: Passing or overtaking a moving vehicle is done, except in special cases, on the _________, with the vehicle returning to its original lane after the manoeuvre.

options.a: Right.
options.b: Left.
options.c: Shoulder.
options.d: On the right or left.

explanation: You overtake on the left. That is the general rule. Exceptions exist, but the question asks for the rule. Overtaking on the shoulder is not allowed.
trap: Option d «derecha o izquierda» (right or left) also contains izquierda. But the rule is only «izquierda» (left). The words «salvo excepciones» already cover the rare cases.

text: If a driver is taking medication and feels sleepy because of it, what must he do?

options.a: Drive normally.
options.b: Drive slowly.
options.c: Refrain from driving.
options.d: Drive with a co-driver.

gist: Sleepy from medication: drive or not
explanation: A sleepy driver is as dangerous as a drunk one. Driving slowly or having a helper does not fix it. The only right answer is not to drive at all.
trap: Three options start with «manejar» (drive). The right one is the only one without it: «abstenerse» (refrain).

text.es: Si un conductor está tomando medicamentos
text.tr: If a driver is taking medication
and because of it feels sleepy,

text: Which documents must be carried compulsorily while driving the vehicle and shown when the competent authority requests them:

options.a: Identity document, valid SOAT (may be virtual) and the vehicle identification card.
options.b: Technical Inspection Certificate and the vehicle purchase contract.
options.c: The vehicle purchase contract.
options.d: All the options are correct.

explanation: Carry: ID, SOAT and the vehicle card (tarjeta de propiedad). The purchase contract is never required. So «all options» is wrong.

text: On stretches of a road with a steep slope that allow only one vehicle to pass, keep in mind that the vehicle going up, compared with the vehicle going down:

options.a: Does not have right of way.
options.b: Has right of way.
options.c: Must stop.
options.d: Must reverse.

gist: Who has priority on narrow steep slope
explanation: On a narrow steep stretch, the vehicle going up has priority. The one going down can stop and reverse more easily. So the descending vehicle gives way.
trap: Options a and b differ only by the word «No» (not). The right one has no «No»: «Tiene preferencia» (has right of way).

se debe de tener en cuenta que

text: When changing direction, a driver must:

options.a: Signal the whole manoeuvre until it is completed.
options.b: Change direction and then signal.
options.c: There is no obligation.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: You signal before the manoeuvre and keep signalling until it ends. Signalling after the turn is useless. The obligation always exists.
trap: Option b «y luego señalizar» (and then signal) is a trap about the order. Correct: signal «toda la maniobra» (the whole manoeuvre), start to finish.

text: Can you drive a vehicle with the engine in neutral?

options.a: Yes, but only if going down a slope.
options.b: No, it is prohibited.
options.c: Yes, provided the driver is not a novice.
options.d: It is not regulated in the regulations.

gist: Driving in neutral: allowed or not
explanation: Driving in neutral is prohibited. It is especially dangerous downhill: the car brakes worse. No exceptions, not for slopes, not for experienced drivers.
trap: Option a «solo si está bajando» (only when going down) sounds logical, but it is a trap. The answer: «prohibido» (prohibited) always.

text: To turn or change lane to the right, the driver must use the turn indicators and, in cases of force majeure, the following hand signal:

options.a: Left arm, forearm and hand extended out of the vehicle.
options.b: Left forearm and hand extended upward outside the vehicle, forming a right angle with the arm.
options.c: Right arm, forearm and hand extended out of the vehicle.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: Hand signal for a right turn
explanation: The driver sits on the left, so signals with the left arm. Right turn: forearm up, at a right angle. A straight arm out means a left turn.
trap: Option a is the left arm «hacia afuera» (straight out): that is the left-turn signal. Option c is «derecho» (right arm): not visible from the window. Correct: «hacia arriba» (upward).

text: If the driving licence is not valid, the vehicles that this licence authorises you to drive:

options.a: May not be driven.
options.b: May be driven only in urban areas.
options.c: May be driven for up to 90 days after the licence expires.
options.d: May be driven normally until you renew your licence.

explanation: An expired licence is like no licence. You may not drive anywhere, not even one day. There is no 90-day or grace period.
trap: Three options start with «Podrán» (may). The right one is the only «No podrán» (may not). Numbers like «90 días» are bait.

text.es: los vehículos que autoriza a conducir

c.es: a la pérdida de vigencia de la licencia.

text: According to the points-based driving licence control system:

options.a: Certain offences add points.
options.b: An offence may add or reduce points, at the offender's choice.
options.c: Certain offences subtract points.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: In Peru points accumulate, they are not deducted. Every offence adds points. Reach 100 and the licence is suspended. The offender chooses nothing.
trap: Options a and c differ by one verb: «suman» (add) is right, «restan» (subtract) is wrong. In Peru points go up, not down.

text: What is the consequence of accumulating 100 points on the driving licence in a period of 24 months?

options.a: Suspension of the driving licence.
options.b: Cancellation of the National Registration Plate.
options.c: Permanent disqualification from obtaining a driving licence.
options.d: Impounding of the vehicle.

explanation: 100 points in two years means the licence is suspended. It is temporary, not permanent. Permanent disqualification comes only after repeated accumulations.
trap: Option c «inhabilitación definitiva» (permanent disqualification) sounds similar, but it is too harsh. The first 100 points bring only «suspensión» (suspension).

c.es: para obtener una licencia de conducir.

text: A lane (carril) is understood to be:

options.a: The part of the road intended for pedestrian traffic.
options.b: The part of the roadway intended for the traffic of a single line of vehicles.
options.c: A rural road intended for pedestrians and animals.
options.d: All the options are correct.

explanation: A carril is a strip of the roadway for one line of vehicles. The part of the road for pedestrians is the pavement (vereda). The animals option is a different concept.
trap: Look for «calzada» (roadway) and «fila de vehículos» (line of vehicles). Options with «peatones» (pedestrians) are not about lanes.

text: A stop line (línea de parada) is understood to be:

options.a: The transverse line marked on the roadway before the intersection, which shows the driver the limit for stopping the vehicle.
options.b: The lines found in parking places.
options.c: The place used for boarding and alighting passengers.
options.d: All the options are correct.

explanation: A stop line is a transverse stripe before the intersection. The vehicle must stop before it. Parking lines and bus stops are something else.
trap: Option d «todas» (all) is a trap. Look for «línea transversal» (transverse line) and «límite para detener» (limit for stopping).

text.es: Se entiende por línea de parada
text.tr: A stop line is understood as

options.a: Narrowing of the roadway on the right side.
options.b: Narrowing of the roadway on the left side.
options.c: Narrowing of the roadway on both sides.
options.d: Widening of the roadway on both sides.

gist: Sign P-17A: road narrows both sides
explanation: The sign shows the road narrowing on both sides. It is a narrowing, not a widening. The one-side options belong to other P-17 signs.
trap: You need two words together: «Reducción» (narrowing) and «ambos lados» (both sides). Option d has «ambos lados» but «Ensanchamiento» (widening) is wrong.

text: If you find a double yellow line made of one solid line and one broken line on a two-way road, what should you do?

options.a: You may overtake in both directions.
options.b: Overtaking is not allowed in either direction.
options.c: Follow the line on your side (if it is solid, do not overtake; if it is broken, overtaking is allowed).
options.d: Follow the line on your side (if it is broken, do not overtake; if it is solid, overtaking is allowed)

gist: Double yellow line: solid plus broken
explanation: Look at the line on your side. Solid means no overtaking. Broken means you may overtake. Option d says the opposite.
trap: Options c and d look almost the same. The right one says «si es continua, no adelantar» (if solid, do not overtake). Option d swaps them.

text: A "zona rígida" (rigid zone) is defined as:

options.a: Area where vehicle traffic is prohibited.
options.b: Area where pedestrian traffic is prohibited.
options.c: Area of the road where parking vehicles is prohibited.
options.d: All options are correct.

explanation: A zona rígida is a stretch of road where parking is prohibited. Driving and walking there are fine. So "all options" is wrong.

text: When the traffic police officer stands facing you or with his back to you, it means:

options.a: Whoever faces him this way must stop.
options.b: Continue driving in the left lane of the road.
options.c: Continue driving.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: Officer facing you or back turned
explanation: The officer's chest or back toward you works like a red light. You must stop. You may go when he stands sideways to you.

text: If there is no speed limit sign, the maximum speed in urban areas on streets (calles y jirones) is:

options.a: 30 km/h.
options.b: 40 km/h.
options.c: 60 km/h.
options.d: 80 km/h.

explanation: On ordinary streets and "jirones" it is 40 km/h. On avenues (avenidas) it is 60. On expressways (vías expresas) it is 80. In school zones it is 30.

options.a: 30 km/h.
options.b: 40 km/h.
options.c: 60 km/h.
options.d: 80 km/h.

explanation: On avenues (avenidas) it is 60 km/h. On ordinary streets it is 40. On expressways it is 80.

options.a: 60 km/h.

options.c: 80 km/h.

explanation: On urban expressways (vías expresas) it is 80 km/h. That is the highest urban limit. 100 km/h applies only on highways (carreteras).

explanation: On highways (carreteras) cars, pickups and motorcycles may go 100 km/h. Buses and trucks have lower limits. 80 is the urban expressway limit.

explanation: The minimum is half the maximum for that road. Street 40 → minimum 20. Highway 100 → minimum 50. The rule gives no fixed number.

text: What is the penalty for driving with blood alcohol above the Penal Code limit, or under the effect of drugs confirmed by a test, or for refusing the test, when the driver was involved in a traffic accident?

options.a: A fine.
options.b: Cancellation of the driving licence.
options.c: Suspension of the driving licence.
options.d: A fine, cancellation of the licence and a permanent ban on getting a licence.

explanation: The key word is "accidente" (accident). Alcohol or drugs plus an accident gets the harshest penalty. Fine, licence cancelled and a lifetime ban. Without an accident it is a fine and a 3-year suspension.
trap: Option b also mentions cancellation, but it is only part. The right answer is the full set: «Multa, cancelación... e inhabilitación definitiva».

options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: Here there was no accident. The penalty is a fine plus a 3-year licence suspension. A fine alone or suspension alone is incomplete. With an accident it would be cancellation.

options.b: From the fourth year, counted from the year after manufacture.

explanation: A new private M1 car skips inspection for its first years. The first inspection is from the fourth year after the year of manufacture. Remember: "cuarto" = fourth.

explanation: SOAT is the compulsory accident insurance. It is valid for 1 year, then you must renew it. Driving without SOAT is not allowed.

text: If a traffic accident happens, what must the driver, the vehicle owner or the transport operator do?

options.b: Notify only the insurance company.
options.c: Notify the insurance company and file a report at the nearest police station.
options.d: Notify only the National Police of Peru.

explanation: After an accident you must do two things. Notify the insurer and report at the police station. Options with "solo" and "únicamente" (only) are incomplete.

options.a: Turn on the hazard warning lights.
options.b: Stop where you are.

options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: First turn on the hazard lights so others see you. Then move the car to the side. Stopping in the road or jumping out is dangerous.

text: May you use your horn to warn the driver ahead that you are going to overtake?

options.a: Yes, as long as the sound is not shrill.
options.b: Yes, unless a sign expressly prohibits it.
options.c: No, it is prohibited.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: In Peru the horn is only for avoiding danger. Honking to announce an overtake is prohibited. Both "Sí" options are traps.
trap: Options a and b start with «Sí» (yes) and sound reasonable. The right one is «No, está prohibido» (no, it is prohibited).

text: If an ambulance approaches without its special lights on and without a siren, it is correct to say that:

options.a: We are not required to give it right of way.
options.b: We must give it priority because it is an ambulance.
options.c: It is signalling that it is on an emergency call.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: An ambulance has priority only with its lights and siren on. Without them it is an ordinary vehicle. You do not have to yield.
trap: Option b sounds "right", but the key is «sin sirena» (without siren). The right answer starts with «No estamos obligados» (not required).

options.c: Get out of the vehicle and confront the offender.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: Green light but intersection still busy
explanation: Green does not mean "go no matter what". Wait until the intersection is clear. Honking or arguing is not the answer.

explanation: A yellow line separates opposite directions. A white line separates lanes in the same direction. Order matters: yellow first, then white.

text: If a line of schoolchildren crosses the road outside the pedestrian crossing, what should you do?

options.a: Warn with the horn.
options.b: Warn by shouting.
options.c: Stop and give way.
options.d: Continue driving slowly.

explanation: Always give way to schoolchildren, even outside the crossing. Stop and let them pass. Honking, shouting or creeping forward is wrong.

text: If you approach a school zone, what should you do?

options.a: You have no obligation if there are no signs.
options.b: Reduce speed to 40 km/h.
options.c: Reduce speed to 30 km/h.
options.d: Reduce speed to 35 km/h.

explanation: In a school zone slow down to 30 km/h. This applies even without a sign. 40 and 35 are traps.

text: Their purpose is to inform road users about limitations, prohibitions or restrictions on the use of the road.

options.a: Regulatory signs.
options.b: Warning signs.
options.c: Information signs.
options.d: Horizontal signs (road markings).

explanation: Prohibitions and restrictions are "reguladoras" (regulatory) signs. "Preventivas" warn about dangers. "Informativas" give information: directions, places.

options.a: Regulatory signs.
options.b: Warning signs.
options.c: Information signs.

explanation: Warning signs (preventivas) tell you about a hazard ahead. Regulatory signs order or forbid. Information signs show directions and services.
trap: «Preventivas» means warning (prevenir – to warn). «Reguladoras» are orders and bans, «informativas» give information.

text: A traffic offence is:

options.a: Not stopping completely at a PARE (STOP) sign.
options.b: Throwing, leaving or abandoning objects or substances on the public road that hinder traffic.
options.c: Using the horn to attract attention unnecessarily.
options.d: All the options are correct.

gist: What counts as a traffic offence
explanation: All three actions are offences. Not stopping at PARE, littering the road and honking without need are all forbidden. So the right answer is “All the options”.
trap: Each of a, b and c is true on its own. When all are true, pick «Todas las alternativas son correctas» (all the options are correct).

text: What should the driver do when approaching a “CEDA EL PASO” (yield) sign at an intersection?

options.a: Give way to emergency vehicles.
options.b: Keep the speed and proceed with care.
options.c: Slow down, stop if necessary and give way to pedestrians or vehicles travelling on the cross road.
options.d: Stop completely and then proceed with care.

gist: What to do at a yield sign
explanation: “Ceda el paso” means give way to traffic on the cross road. Slow down and stop only if needed. A full stop is required only at a PARE sign.
trap: Option d («Parar totalmente» – stop completely) describes the PARE sign, not CEDA EL PASO.

text: You must not drive a vehicle:

options.a: If you do not have SOAT (compulsory insurance).
options.b: In reverse, except for the exceptions set by the rules.
options.c: If you do not have a licence for the type of vehicle you want to drive.
options.d: All are correct.

explanation: Driving without SOAT or without the right licence category is not allowed. Reversing is also banned, except where the rules allow it. All three points are true.
trap: All three options are real bans. Do not pick just one; the answer is «Todas son correctas» (all are correct).

text: What should you do if you approach an intersection with no traffic light and no traffic police present, and you see a pedestrian crossing on the pedestrian crossing?

options.a: Slow down and pass carefully.
options.b: Stop the vehicle and give way to the pedestrian.
options.c: Continue because you have priority.
options.d: Speed up to get through the crossing before the pedestrian.

explanation: A pedestrian on the crossing has priority. You must stop and let them cross. Just slowing down (option a) is not enough.

text: About the use of the seat belt in vehicles in circulation, it is correct to say that:

options.c: Seat belt use is not only mandatory for the driver.
options.d: All the options are correct.

gist: Who must wear a seat belt
explanation: In front, belts are mandatory for everyone. In the back, when fitted from the factory or required by rules. So belts are not only for the driver. All three statements are true.
trap: Option c with «no solo» (not only) sounds odd, but it is true: passengers must buckle up too. All three are true – «Todas las alternativas son correctas».

options.c: The driver must use the horn only to avoid dangerous situations.

explanation: The horn is only for avoiding danger. Honking without need is an offence, so b is wrong. Option a is too soft: “try not to use” is not the rule.
