options.c: Keep the vehicle's engine running.
options.d: All the options are correct.

explanation: When refuelling nobody may smoke, neither driver nor passengers. The engine must be off, and passengers should get out. So a and c are wrong, and “All the options” is wrong too.
trap: «Todas las alternativas» is wrong here: a and c are mistakes. Only b is right: «Abstenerse de fumar» (refrain from smoking).

text: While you are driving your motor vehicle, can you let a cyclist hold on to your car while riding the bicycle?

options.a: Yes, as long as the cyclist holds on to the rear of the car, but never to its side.
options.b: Yes, as long as all the relevant safety measures are taken.
options.c: Yes, as long as this is done at a speed not higher than
options.d: No, it is a prohibited action and whoever does it can be punished with a fine.

gist: Can a cyclist hold onto your car
explanation: A cyclist must never hold on to a moving car. It is banned always, with no conditions. There is a fine for it.
trap: Three options start with «Sí, siempre y cuando» (yes, as long as…). But there are no conditions – the only «No» is correct.

a.es: se sujete a la parte posterior
a.tr: holds on to the rear part

a.es: pero nunca a la parte lateral
a.tr: but never to the side part

d.tr: No, it is a prohibited action

text: If you want to hold a race between your vehicle and another motor vehicle, for that you can use:

options.a: The streets around the park in the district where you live, between 11:00 pm and 5:00 am.
options.b: A racing circuit, autodrome or drag strip authorised by the competent authority.
options.c: The streets around the park in the district where you live, as long as you have the corresponding municipal permit.
options.d: All the options are correct.

explanation: Racing on ordinary streets is banned – at night or with a permit too. Only on a special circuit or autodrome authorised by the authorities.
trap: Options a and c add conditions (night, permit), but streets are still not allowed. Look for «autódromo» (autodrome).

a.es: del distrito en el cual reside,
a.tr: of the district where you live,

c.es: del distrito en el cual reside,
c.tr: of the district where you live,

text: Indicate which of the following behaviours is a traffic offence:

options.a: Having the vehicle's door, bonnet or boot open while the vehicle is moving.
options.b: Driving a vehicle slowly in the left lane causing congestion.
options.c: Driving a vehicle with the engine in neutral or switched off.
options.d: All the options are correct.

explanation: All three actions are banned. An open door or bonnet while moving is an offence. Driving slowly on the left is an offence. So is coasting in neutral or with the engine off.
trap: Option c seems harmless (coasting in neutral), but it is also an offence. All three are true – «Todas las alternativas son correctas».

a.es: Tener la puerta, capot o maletera
a.tr: Having the door, bonnet or boot

a.es: cuando el vehículo está en marcha.

b.es: por el carril de la izquierda

c.es: con el motor en punto neutro

text: Markings on the pavement are an essential element for vehicle operation, since their function is:

options.a: To replace vertical signs when they are not on the road; for that reason they are placed where there are no vertical signs.
options.b: To guide road users only on roads that have hazards.
options.c: To regulate traffic, as well as warn and guide road users.
options.d: All the options are correct.

explanation: Markings regulate, warn and guide. They complement signs, they do not replace them. And they work everywhere, not only on dangerous roads.
trap: a («reemplazar» – replace) and b («únicamente» – only) contain false limits. c is right: «Reglamentar... advertir y guiar».

a.es: cuando ésta no se encuentra en la vía,
a.tr: when they are not on the road,
for that reason they are placed
where there are no vertical signs.

c.es: y guiar a los usuarios de la vía.

text: Pavement markings of __________ colour complement information signs, for example parking areas for people with reduced mobility.

options.a: White.
options.b: Blue.
options.c: Red.
options.d: Grey.

explanation: Blue markings complement information signs. Example: parking for people with disabilities. White and yellow are for normal traffic lines.

text: The central yellow line on the pavement is continuous when:

options.a: It is not allowed to cross into the other lane.
options.b: It is allowed to cross into the other lane for overtaking.
options.c: It is a two-way road that allows crossing into the other lane.
options.d: It separates traffic flows in the same direction.

explanation: A continuous yellow line is a border you must not cross. A broken yellow line allows overtaking. Yellow separates opposite flows, not same-direction flows.
trap: a and b differ by one word: «No está permitido» (not allowed) is right; «Está permitido» (allowed) is wrong. Continuous = no crossing.

a.tr: to cross into the other lane.

b.tr: to cross into the other lane

text: If a driver travelling in the right lane comes across the slanted arrows shown in the picture, the correct behaviour is:

options.a: Continue driving in the lane he is in.
options.b: Overtake the vehicle ahead of him that is travelling in the left lane.
options.c: Not overtake the vehicle ahead that is in the left lane and continue in his lane.
options.d: Change to the left lane with caution.

explanation: Slanted arrows warn that the right lane is about to end. You must move left early and carefully. Staying in your lane (a, c) is wrong – it disappears.
trap: a and c suggest «continuar por su carril» (stay in your lane). But the arrows mean the lane merges: look for «Cambiarse» (change lane).

text.es: que circula por el carril derecho
text.tr: who travels in the right lane

text.es: que se muestran en la figura,

a.es: por el carril en que se encuentra.
a.tr: in the lane he is in.

b.es: que se encuentra delante de él
y que circula por el carril izquierdo.
b.tr: and travels in the left lane.

c.es: y que circula por el carril izquierdo
c.tr: and travels in the left lane

text: If, while driving, a Traffic Police officer asks the driver to take a breathalyser test, the correct action of the driver is:

options.a: Take the breathalyser test, since he is obliged to do so at the request of the Traffic Police officer.
options.b: Take or refuse the breathalyser test, since taking the test is not an obligation of the driver.
options.c: Refuse the breathalyser test, since it is only required if he has been involved in a traffic accident.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: If the police ask, the driver must take the alcohol test. Refusing is a serious offence. The test is not tied only to accidents.
trap: a and b both start with «Someterse…». Look for «está obligado» (is obliged) – that is a. «no constituye una obligación» (is not an obligation) is false.

text.es: un efectivo de la Policía de Tránsito
someterse a una prueba de alcoholemia;
la acción correcta del conductor es:
text.tr: the correct action of the driver is:

a.es: Someterse a la prueba de alcoholemia,
ya que está obligado a ello
a.tr: since he is obliged to do so
at the request of the officer

b.es: ya que no constituye una obligación
b.tr: since it is not an obligation

c.es: Negarse a la prueba de alcoholemia,

text: Which of the following behaviours is NOT a traffic offence?

options.a: Carrying the number plates in the wrong place.
options.b: Following emergency and official vehicles in order to move faster.
options.c: Throwing objects on the public road that hinder traffic.
options.d: Stopping completely at a PARE sign when there are no pedestrians and/or vehicles on the cross road.

explanation: The question asks what is NOT an offence. At a PARE sign you must always stop fully – even if nobody is there. That is correct behaviour, not an offence. a, b and c are offences.
trap: Note «no es» (is not) in the question. Three options are offences; look for the correct action: «Detenerse totalmente» (stop completely).

a.es: en el lugar que no corresponde.

b.es: Seguir a los vehículos de emergencia

text: If a driver leaves his property and has to cross the pavement to enter a road, the correct behaviour is:

options.a: Give way only to the vehicles on the road, but not to pedestrians.
options.b: Give way to the vehicles on the road and to the pedestrians on the pavement.
options.c: Sound the horn to warn pedestrians on the pavement to stop.
options.d: Drive out quickly, to avoid accidents.

gist: Leaving a driveway across the pavement
explanation: A driver leaving a property has priority over nobody. He gives way both to vehicles on the road and to pedestrians on the pavement. Honking to make pedestrians stop is not allowed.
trap: a and b look alike. a has «solo… pero no a los peatones» (only… but not to pedestrians) – wrong. b is right: vehicles «y a los peatones» (and pedestrians).

text.es: y tiene que cruzar la acera
text.tr: and has to cross the pavement

b.es: y a los peatones que circulan por la acera.
b.tr: and to the pedestrians walking on the pavement.

text: What does a continuous white line painted between the right lane and the shoulder (berma) of a highway mean?

options.a: A lane for motorcycles.
options.b: A line dividing the pedestrian area and the vehicle area.
options.c: A line that can be crossed to overtake in case of congestion.
options.d: That you must not drive across it, unless there is an emergency situation.

gist: White line next to the shoulder
explanation: The shoulder (berma) is not a driving lane. The continuous line before it forbids driving onto it. The only exception is an emergency.
trap: Option c («puede cruzarse para rebasar» – can be crossed to overtake) is wrong: the shoulder is not for overtaking. Look for «emergencia» (emergency).

text.es: pintada entre el carril de la derecha

c.tr: A line that can be crossed

text: If you drive at night, there is fog and you have fog lights, you must use:

options.a: Low beams together with the fog lights.
options.b: Only high beams.
options.c: Only low beams.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: In fog, high beams reflect off the fog and blind you. Turn on low beams and fog lights together. Only low beams (c) is worse when you have fog lights.
trap: c («Solo las luces bajas» – only low beams) looks right, but the question says you have fog lights: use them «junto con» (together with) low beams.

text: In the case shown in the picture, can the red vehicle overtake the blue one?

options.a: It can, if no vehicle is coming in the opposite direction.
options.b: It can only if the oncoming vehicle is far away and the manoeuvre can be done safely.
options.c: It cannot.
options.d: It can, on the left.

gist: Overtaking across a solid yellow line
explanation: In the picture, the line on the red car's side is solid yellow. A solid line must not be crossed to overtake. Even with no oncoming traffic, it is still not allowed.
trap: Options a, b and d start with «Puede» (it can) and add conditions. With a solid line there are no conditions: the only answer is «No puede hacerlo» (it cannot).

text: The following sign (R-17) means:

options.a: No parking.
options.b: Motor vehicles prohibited.
options.c: Private cars prohibited.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: A red circle with a crossed-out car bans all motor vehicles. Not only private cars. Parking is banned by a different sign, with the letter E.
trap: b and c look alike: «vehículos automotores» (motor vehicles – all of them) is broader than «autos particulares» (private cars). The broad one, b, is right.

text: If you are driving your vehicle along a road and before crossing the intersection you come across sign R-4, it tells you:

options.a: That the street is closed.
options.b: That you are about to enter a road going the opposite way and must not enter.
options.c: That you must stop completely before you can enter.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct

explanation: R-4 'NO ENTRE' means 'do not enter'. The road ahead carries traffic coming towards you. You must not enter it. It does not close the street and does not ask you to stop.
trap: Option c says 'debe parar' (must stop): that is the PARE sign (R-1), not R-4. R-4 simply forbids entering.

b.tr: That you are about to enter

text: The following sign (P-36) means:

options.a: A tunnel ahead.
options.b: Slippery surface.
options.c: Switch on the low beams.
options.d: Keep a safe distance between vehicles.

explanation: The sign shows a skidding car with wavy tyre tracks. P-36 warns of a slippery surface (superficie deslizante). Slow down and avoid hard braking.

text: The following sign (R-14) means:

options.a: Drive in the right-hand lane.
options.b: Drive in the centre lane.
options.c: Drive only in the direction shown by the arrow.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: R-14 'CIRCULACIÓN' with an arrow: traffic goes only where the arrow points. It is not about choosing a lane. The key word in the answer is 'flecha' (arrow).

text: If you are driving along a road and come across sign (R-11a), it tells you:

options.a: That it is a three-lane one-way road.
options.b: That it is a three-lane road and you may use only one of them.
options.c: That it is a three-lane road and you may use the two on the right.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: The sign shows three arrows. Two point up on the right, one points down on the left. The two right lanes are yours; the left one is for oncoming traffic. So you may use the two lanes on the right.
trap: Option a says 'un solo sentido' (one-way) and b says 'solo uno' (only one): both wrong. One arrow points down, so there is oncoming traffic, and you get two lanes.

text: The following sign (R-30c) means:

options.a: That the maximum speed on the road is 50 km/h.
options.b: That the minimum speed on the road is 50 km/h.
options.c: That when exiting the road you are driving on, the maximum speed is 50 km/h.
options.d: That when exiting the road you are driving on, the minimum speed is 50 km/h.

explanation: The sign says 'SALIDA' (exit) above the number. The 50 km/h limit applies on the exit, not on the whole road. A red circle with a number is a maximum (máxima), not a minimum.
trap: Look for two words together: 'al salir' (when exiting) and 'máxima' (maximum). Option a lacks 'salir'; option d says 'mínima' (minimum).

text: The following sign (R-5-4) means:

options.a: That the road does not continue and drivers must turn left.
options.b: That the intersection provides for left turns in both directions.
options.c: That the intersection is under maintenance and for now you can only turn left.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: The sign shows two left arrows from opposite directions and the word 'SOLO'. Each direction may only turn left. It is a normal junction sign, not roadworks and not a dead end.
trap: Options a and c also talk about 'girar a la izquierda' (turn left). The right one is marked by 'ambos sentidos' (both directions).

text: The following sign (R-9) means:

options.a: That making a U-turn is not permitted.
options.b: That a U-turn is permitted.
options.c: That you may turn left if you wish.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: The sign shows a U-turn arrow in a red circle with no line through it. Without the red slash the sign allows, it does not prohibit. So a U-turn (giro en U) is permitted here.
trap: Options a and b differ only by the word 'no'. The right one is 'está permitido' (is permitted) without 'no'. A slash through the arrow would mean prohibited.

text: The following sign (R-5-2) means:

options.a: That the road only allows turning left.
options.b: Warning of a fork in the road.
options.c: That the lane you are in allows you to turn left or go straight ahead.
options.d: It is not a valid sign in Peru.

explanation: The arrow on the sign splits in two: straight ahead and left. From this lane you may go straight or turn left. Option a is wrong because of 'solo' (only): going straight is also allowed.

text: The following sign (R-20) means:

options.a: That a pedestrian must look for cars coming from the right before crossing.
options.b: That the driver coming from the right must watch out for pedestrians.
options.c: That pedestrians must walk on the left.
options.d: That pedestrians must walk on the right.

explanation: The sign shows a pedestrian and an arrow pointing left. R-20 tells pedestrians to walk on the left side. This way they see oncoming cars. The answer is c, with 'izquierda' (left).
trap: Options c and d differ by one word: 'izquierda' (left) and 'derecha' (right). The arrow on the sign points left.

text: The following sign (R-40) means:

options.a: Zebra crossing.
options.b: Police checkpoint.
options.c: Slippery pavement.
options.d: Drive with the low beams on.

explanation: The sign shows a headlamp with light beams in a red circle. R-40 requires you to drive with the low beams on (luces bajas). It is often placed before tunnels.

text: The following sign (R-48) means:

options.a: Pedestrians must walk on the right and trucks drive on the left
options.b: Pedestrians must be careful with trucks.
options.c: Loading and unloading zone.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: The sign shows a truck and a person carrying a load. R-48 marks a loading and unloading zone (carga y descarga). It is not about pedestrians or which side to use.

text: The following sign (R-49) means:

options.a: Changing lanes to the left and to the right is permitted.
options.b: You must keep a safe distance between vehicles.
options.c: Changing lanes to the left to overtake is permitted.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: The sign shows two cars one behind the other with distance marks between them. R-49 requires keeping a safe distance (distancia de seguridad). It does not permit changing lanes.

text: The following sign (R-50) means:

options.a: That if there is only one lane, the driver who arrived first has right of way.
options.b: That if there is only one lane, the driver looking at the sign has right of way.
options.c: That if there is only one lane, the driver looking at the sign has no right of way and must give way to oncoming traffic.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: The sign shows a big black arrow down and a small red arrow up. It reads 'Preferencia al sentido contrario' (priority to oncoming traffic). Whoever sees this sign gives way to oncoming cars on the narrow section.
trap: Option b says 'tiene preferencia' (has priority); the right one, c, says 'no tiene preferencia' (has no priority). Look for 'darle paso al del sentido contrario' (give way to oncoming).

b.tr: who is looking at the sign.

text: Sign (R-5-1) is:

options.a: An informative sign.
options.b: A warning sign.
options.c: A mandatory sign (obligation).
options.d: It is not a valid sign in Peru.

gist: What type of sign R-5-1 is
explanation: R-5-1: a left arrow and the word 'SOLO' (only). R-series signs are white with black and red: regulatory signs. This one orders you: left turn only. So it is a mandatory sign (obligación).
trap: 'Preventiva' (warning) signs are the yellow diamonds of the P series. 'Informativa' signs are blue and green. A white sign with a black arrow and 'SOLO' is an obligation.

text: Sign (P-3a) tells the driver that:

options.a: There is a curve and counter-curve to the left.
options.b: There is a curve and counter-curve to the right.
options.c: There is a sharp curve and counter-curve to the right.
options.d: There is a sharp curve and counter-curve to the left.

explanation: The arrow on the sign has sharp angles: first right, then left. Sharp angles mean 'pronunciada' (sharp). The first bend goes right, so 'a la derecha'.
trap: All four options look almost the same. You need two words together: 'pronunciada' (sharp) and 'derecha' (right). A smooth arrow without angles would have no 'pronunciada'.

text: The following sign (P-5-1a) warns the driver that:

options.a: You are approaching a curve and counter-curve to the left.
options.b: You are approaching a curve and counter-curve to the right.
options.c: You are approaching a winding road to the right.
options.d: You are approaching a winding road to the left.

explanation: The arrow on the sign has three or more bends. That is a 'camino sinuoso' (winding road), not just two curves. The first bend goes left, so 'a la izquierda'.
trap: Two pairs of options: 'curva y contra-curva' (two curves) and 'camino sinuoso' (winding road). Many bends = sinuoso. Then look at the first bend: left (izquierda).

text: The following sign (P-61) warns the driver that:

options.a: The direction of traffic is the one the arrow shows.
options.b: You are approaching a narrowing of the road on both sides.
options.c: You are driving through a horizontal curve.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: P-61 is a yellow panel with a black chevron. These panels are placed along a bend to show its line. The chevron does not set the traffic direction; it marks the curve of the road.

text: The following sign (P-34) warns the driver that:

options.a: The road is in bad condition and has potholes.
options.b: You are approaching a bump.
options.c: You are approaching a speed bump.
options.d: You are approaching a dip (badén).

explanation: The sign shows a black bar that dips down. That is a 'badén': a dip in the road, often for water drainage. A bump going up would be 'resalto' or 'rompe muelles'.
trap: 'Resalto' and 'rompe muelles' are bumps going up. 'Badén' is a dip going down, as on the sign.

text: The following sign (P-60) is:

options.a: A tourist sign.
options.b: An informative sign.
options.c: A warning sign.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

gist: What type of sign P-60 is
explanation: P-60 is a yellow triangle reading 'NO ADELANTAR' (no overtaking). Yellow colour and the letter P mean 'preventiva' (warning). It warns that a no-overtaking zone begins.

text: The following sign (P-46) indicates:

options.a: Presence of a cycle lane.
options.b: Authorisation for cyclists to cross.
options.c: Cyclists on the road.
options.d: A cycle lane nearby.

explanation: The sign shows only a bicycle, with no lines and no arrow. P-46 warns that cyclists may be on the road. Other signs, P-46A and P-46B, are about a cycle lane (ciclovía).
trap: The three wrong options contain 'ciclovía' (cycle lane) or 'cruce' (crossing). The right one is simply 'ciclistas en la vía' (cyclists on the road).

text: The following sign (P-46-a) indicates:

options.a: That cyclists must use the cycle lane.
options.b: That we are approaching a cycle-lane crossing.
options.c: That the cycle lane is only for cyclists.
options.d: All the alternatives are correct.

explanation: The sign shows a bicycle and dashed crossing lines. P-46A warns that a cycle-lane crossing is ahead. Without a down arrow the sign means 'approaching', not 'here'.
trap: Options a and c are rules for cyclists, but the sign is addressed to the driver. Do not pick 'Todas' (all): only b is right.

text: The following sign (P-46b) indicates:

options.a: That cyclists must stop at that point.
options.b: That we are approaching a cycle-lane crossing.
options.c: That the cycle lane is only for cyclists.
options.d: The location of a cyclist crossing.

explanation: Under the sign there is an arrow pointing down. The down arrow means the cyclist crossing is right here. Without the arrow (P-46A) the sign says 'approaching'.
trap: Option b says 'nos aproximamos' (we are approaching): that is P-46A without the arrow. With the down arrow the right word is 'ubicación' (location).

text: The following sign (P-48) indicates:

options.a: The road is for pedestrians only.
options.b: Area with pedestrians present.
options.c: Location of a school crossing.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: The sign shows a walking pedestrian, with no crossing lines and no arrow. P-48 warns that pedestrians may be on the road here. It is not a pedestrian-only road and not a school crossing.
trap: Option a says 'uso exclusivo' (pedestrians only); that is a different sign. The right one is 'presencia de peatones' (presence of pedestrians).

text: The following sign (P-48a) indicates:

options.a: The road is for pedestrians only.
options.b: A pedestrian crossing ahead.
options.c: Location of a school crossing.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: The sign shows a pedestrian on crossing lines, with no arrow. P-48A warns that a pedestrian crossing is ahead. A down arrow (P-48B) would mean 'the crossing is here'.
trap: 'Cruce peatonal' (pedestrian crossing), not 'cruce escolar' (school crossing). Without the arrow it is 'proximidad' (approaching).

text: The following sign (P-48-b) indicates:

options.a: Location of a school crossing.
options.b: A carriageway ahead.
options.c: Location of a pedestrian crossing.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: It is sign P-48A plus a down arrow. The down arrow means the pedestrian crossing is right here. A school crossing uses a different sign, with two children.
trap: Options a and c start the same way: 'Ubicación de un cruce'. Then 'escolar' (school) is wrong and 'peatonal' (pedestrian) is right.

text: The following sign (P-49) indicates:

options.a: School zone.
options.b: Approach to a pedestrian crossing.
options.c: Busy area.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: P-49 is a yellow-green sign with two schoolchildren. It warns: school zone ahead. Option b talks about a crossing, not a school.
trap: Signs P-49, P-49a and P-49b all show schoolchildren. No zebra stripes and no arrow means «zona escolar» (school zone).

text: The following sign (P-49a) indicates:

options.a: School zone.
options.b: Approach to a school crossing.
options.c: Location of a school crossing.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: On P-49a the schoolchildren walk on zebra stripes. The sign warns: school crossing ahead. «Proximidad» means the crossing is still ahead. The exact spot is shown by P-49b with an arrow.
trap: «Proximidad» (approach) means the crossing is ahead; «Ubicación» (location) means it is right here. P-49a has no arrow, so it is «proximidad».

text: The following sign (P-49b) indicates:

options.a: Busy area.
options.b: Approach to a pedestrian crossing.
options.c: Location of a school crossing
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: P-49b is the same schoolchildren sign, but with a downward arrow. The arrow shows: the crossing is right here. That is «ubicación» (location), not «proximidad» (approach).
trap: Option b says «cruce peatonal» (pedestrian crossing), but the sign shows schoolchildren: a «cruce escolar». The arrow means «ubicación».

text: The following sign (P-50) indicates:

options.a: Sports area.
options.b: Approach to a sports field.
options.c: Approach to an urban area.
options.d: Children playing.

explanation: P-50 shows a child with a ball. The sign warns: children may be playing nearby and can run onto the road. The sign says nothing about sports or a city.

text: The following sign (P-51) indicates:

options.a: Parking area for heavy vehicles.
options.b: Approach to a rural area.
options.c: Farm machinery on the road.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: Sign P-51 shows a tractor. It warns: slow farm machinery may enter the road. It is not a parking area and not just a rural zone.

text: The following sign (P-53) indicates:

options.a: Approach to a stable.
options.b: Approach to a farming area.
options.c: Animals on the road.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: Sign P-53 shows a cow. It warns: there may be animals on the road. Not a stable, not a field: animals on the roadway itself.

text: The following sign (P-55) indicates:

options.a: Broken traffic light.
options.b: Approach to a traffic light.
options.c: Traffic lights in a green wave.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: Sign P-55 shows a traffic light. It warns: traffic light ahead, be ready to stop. The sign does not say the light is broken («malogrado»).

c.tr: Traffic lights in a green wave.

text: The following sign (P-58) tells you:

options.a: That you are approaching a STOP (PARE) sign.
options.b: That you must stop where the P-58 sign is.
options.c: That it is a STOP, but you may keep going.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: P-58 is a yellow sign with an arrow and a small STOP inside. It warns: a STOP sign is ahead. You stop at the real STOP sign, not here.
trap: Option b says stop «donde está la señal P-58» (where the P-58 sign is). No: P-58 only warns; you stop at the real STOP sign.

text: The following sign (P-59) tells you:

options.a: That you are approaching a CEDA EL PASO (yield) sign.
options.b: That you must yield where the P-59 sign is.
options.c: That it is a STOP, but you may keep going.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: P-59 is a yellow sign with a small yield triangle inside. It warns: a CEDA EL PASO sign is ahead. You yield at the real sign, not here. Option c is about STOP, a different sign.
trap: Option b says yield «donde está la señal P-59» (where the P-59 sign is). No: P-59 only warns.

a.es: una señal de CEDA EL PASO.

text: The following sign (P-41) tells you:

options.a: That you are approaching a truck area.
options.b: That you must turn on your lights because you are approaching an area with poor visibility.
options.c: That you are approaching a tunnel.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: Sign P-41 shows a tunnel entrance. It warns: tunnel ahead. Option b sounds sensible, but the sign is specifically about a tunnel.
trap: Option b about lights and «poca visibilidad» (poor visibility) makes sense in a tunnel, but it is not the sign's meaning. Look for the word «túnel».

text: The following sign (P-45) indicates:

options.a: Approach to an airport.
options.b: Approach to an aircraft runway.
options.c: Aircraft flying at low altitude.
options.d: Aircraft that make noise.

explanation: Sign P-45 shows an aeroplane. It warns: aircraft fly low here, which can distract or startle you. The sign says nothing about an airport, a runway or noise.
trap: All options mention aircraft. The right one has «baja altura» (low altitude): that is what the sign means.

text: The following sign (P-52) tells you:

options.a: That you must give priority to ambulances.
options.b: That you must give priority to fire fighters.
options.c: That you are approaching an exit of fire engines.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: Sign P-52 shows a fire engine. It warns: fire engines exit ahead, for example from a fire station. The sign does not order you to yield; it only warns.
trap: Options a and b talk about «prioridad de paso» (priority). P-52 is a warning sign; look for the word «salida» (exit).

text: The following sign (P-66) tells you:

options.a: That you are approaching a desert.
options.b: That you are approaching an area where there are gusts of side wind.
options.c: That you are getting close to an area of sand drifts on the road.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: P-66 shows a palm tree bent by the wind. The sign warns: side wind, hold the wheel firmly. Sand on the road is a different sign, P-66a.
trap: P-66 (palm tree) is «viento lateral» (side wind). P-66a (sand on the road) is «arenamiento». Do not mix up the two signs.

c.tr: That you are getting close to

text: The following sign (P-66a) tells you:

options.a: That you are approaching a storm.
options.b: That you are passing through an area where there are gusts of side wind.
options.c: That you are getting close to an area of sand drifts on the road.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: P-66a shows a road being covered by sand. The sign warns: sand on the roadway, less grip. The palm tree and wind is sign P-66.
trap: «Arenamiento» comes from «arena» (sand). Option b about «viento lateral» (side wind) is the neighbouring sign P-66.

c.tr: That you are getting close to

text: If while driving your vehicle you come across the vertical sign shown, you must understand that:

options.a: The road is closed and you must take the alternative route that the sign shows.
options.b: At the next intersection it is prohibited to turn left, and therefore, if you want to follow that route, you must take the alternative route that the sign shows.
options.c: At the next intersection it is prohibited to turn right, and therefore, if you want to follow that route, you must take the alternative route that the sign shows.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

gist: Sign: no left turn, use detour
explanation: The sign shows a no-left-turn symbol and a detour to avenue Oriente. So you cannot turn left at the intersection; you follow the detour. Option c says «derecha» (right), which is wrong. The road is not closed, so option a is wrong.
trap: Options b and c differ by one word: «izquierda» (left) and «derecha» (right). The sign crosses out the left turn, so b.

b.tr: if you want to follow that route,

c.tr: if you want to follow that route,

text: If while driving your vehicle you come across the vertical sign shown, you must understand that:

options.a: If you want to turn left, you must go past the intersection and go around the block.
options.b: At the next intersection it is prohibited to turn left, and therefore, if you want to follow that route, you must do it one block before.
options.c: In that direction there is a parking area.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

gist: Sign: turn left by circling block
explanation: The arrow on the sign passes the intersection, circles the block and exits left. This is how you turn left where a direct turn is not allowed. Option b says «una cuadra antes» (one block before), which the sign does not show.
trap: Options a and b are both about turning left. The key is «dar la vuelta a la manzana» (go around the block): that is what the arrow draws.

you must go past the intersection

text: The following sign (I-14) means:

options.a: Sign for a hostel.
options.b: Sign for lodging.
options.c: Sign for a hospital.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: I-14 is a blue sign with a big white letter H. It shows: hospital («hospital») nearby. «Hostal» and «hospedaje» mean lodging; the words look similar, but the meaning is different.
trap: Three similar words: «hostal» (hostel), «hospedaje» (lodging), «hospital» (hospital). The letter H on blue is a hospital.

text: The following sign (I-31) means:

options.a: Approach to a taxi bay.
options.b: Approach to a permitted parking place.
options.c: Approach to a parking area for residents.
options.d: Approach to a parking place for emergencies.

explanation: Sign I-31 shows a lay-by at the edge of the road. It is an emergency stopping place: breakdown, feeling unwell. Not taxis, not ordinary parking, not residents' parking.
trap: All options are about parking. The right one has the word «emergencias» (emergencies).

text: The following sign (I-9) means:

options.a: Police control area.
options.b: Customs control area.
options.c: Military area.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: Blue sign I-9 shows a soldier in a helmet. It is the information sign for a military area. Police and customs are different signs. Look for the word «militar».

text: The following sign (I-18) is used to indicate:

options.a: A hardware store nearby.
options.b: A mechanic's workshop nearby.
options.c: A petrol station nearby.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct

explanation: Sign I-18 shows a spanner. It shows: a mechanic's workshop nearby. In Peru «grifo» is a petrol station; «ferretería» is a hardware store.

text: The following sign (I-19) is used to indicate:

options.a: A mechanic's workshop nearby.
options.b: A shop nearby.
options.c: A petrol station nearby.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: Sign I-19 shows a fuel pump. In Peru «grifo» means a petrol station. A spanner is a mechanic (I-18); a tyre is a tyre shop (I-20).

text: The following sign (I-20) is used to indicate:

options.a: A mechanic's workshop nearby.
options.b: An area nearby where you must drive with chains on the tyres.
options.c: A petrol station nearby.
options.d: A tyre shop nearby.

explanation: Sign I-20 shows a tyre. It shows: a tyre shop («llantería») nearby. Option b also mentions «llantas» (tyres), but chains on the tyres is a different sign.
trap: «Llantería» (tyre shop) and «llantas» (tyres) look alike. The blue sign with a tyre is a service, not an order to fit chains.

text: The following sign (R-16a) is used to indicate:

options.a: End of the restriction on motor vehicle traffic.
options.b: End of the «no overtaking» restriction.
options.c: End of the restriction on two-way traffic.
options.d: None of the alternatives is correct.

explanation: R-16a shows two cars crossed by grey lines and the words FIN RESTRICCIÓN. It is the end of the «no overtaking» zone (sign R-16). After it you may overtake again.
trap: All three options start with «Fin de la restricción». Look at the ending: two cars side by side = «adelantar» (overtake).

text: The driver's behaviour as a road user must be oriented towards:

options.a: Value for life.
options.b: Respect for the physical integrity of the other road users.
options.c: Respect for the authority in charge of traffic supervision and discipline.
options.d: All the alternatives are correct.

gist: What driver behaviour is oriented to
explanation: All three points are correct principles of driver behaviour. Value life, protect others' health, respect the authorities: all together. So the right answer is «Todas» (all).
trap: Each of options a, b and c is true on its own; that is the trap. When all three are true, pick «Todas las alternativas son correctas» (all the alternatives are correct).

c.es: la vigilancia y disciplina de tráfico.

text: The following are considered vulnerable road users and therefore deserve special protection:

options.a: Pedestrians, children, older adults, people with reduced mobility, cyclists.
options.b: Only pedestrians and cyclists.
options.c: Only pedestrians and children.
options.d: All the alternatives are correct, except for cyclists.

explanation: Vulnerable users are all those not protected by a car body. That is pedestrians, children, older adults, people with reduced mobility and cyclists. Options with «únicamente» (only) shorten the list; they are wrong.
trap: «Únicamente» (only) signals a trap: the list is incomplete. Option d excludes cyclists, but they are vulnerable too. The right answer is the fullest list.

text: The following sign (P-61) shows:

options.a: Retroreflective arrows that indicate danger.
options.b: Curve delineators, which guide the driver.
options.c: Warning to the driver about a bridge ahead.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: Sign P-61 is a curve delineator. It stands along a bend and shows the driver where the road goes. It is not a danger arrow and not a bridge warning.
trap: Option a «flechas» (arrows) looks similar in the picture, but the right answer is «delineadores de curva» (curve delineators).

text: If you hold a private A-I licence, you are allowed to drive the following vehicle:

options.a: Truck, dump type.
options.b: Bus, panoramic type.
options.c: Mototaxi.
options.d: Car, sedan type.

gist: What an A-I licence lets you drive
explanation: An A-I licence is for cars. Trucks and buses need professional licences (A-II, A-III). A mototaxi is category B.

text: While a person is driving, they are allowed to:

options.a: Share their seat with a child, as long as the child is under one year old.
options.b: Let another person take control of the steering, as long as…
options.c: Drive with one hand on the steering wheel when they need to operate a control, such as changing gears.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: One hand on the wheel is fine when you change gears or use a control. A child on the driver's seat is never allowed. Letting someone else steer is not allowed either.
trap: Options a and b use «siempre y cuando» (as long as) and sound like exceptions, but they are always violations.

text: The driver is ________ to ___________ to the tests requested by the officer of the National Police of Peru assigned to traffic control, to determine intoxication by alcohol, drugs, narcotics or other toxic substances

options.a: Within their right - to refuse.
options.b: Entitled - to reject.
options.c: Obliged - to submit.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: Must the driver take the alcohol test
explanation: The driver must take the alcohol and drug tests when the police ask. Refusing is a very serious offence. Options a and b talk about refusing, which is wrong.

text.es: de la Policía Nacional del Perú,
text.tr: of the National Police of Peru,

text: If a driver has an obvious physical disability that is not listed in the restrictions section of their licence, what happens:

options.a: The Traffic Police stop that driver and the authority that issued the licence orders a re-examination.
options.b: The competent authority issues a special permit for that driver.
options.c: The Traffic Police issue a special permit for that driver.
options.d: The Traffic Police give that driver a reasonable period to keep driving.

gist: Disability not listed on licence: what happens
explanation: The police stop the driver. The authority that issued the licence orders a new exam. Nobody issues a «permiso excepcional» or gives extra time.
trap: Three wrong options offer a «permiso excepcional» (special permit) or a «plazo» (time period). The right one has «intervenga» (stops) and «reexaminación» (re-examination).

text.tr: In the case of a driver

text: Can a person with a physical disability get a private driving licence?

options.a: Yes, as long as the disability can be overcome with a corrective device that is set as one of the restrictions in the current rules.
options.b: No, it is strictly forbidden.
options.c: It depends on the judgement of the licence-issuing centre.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: Yes, it is possible. The disability must be overcome by a corrector: glasses, prosthesis, adapted controls. Then a restriction is written on the licence. It is not forbidden and does not depend on the centre's opinion.

text: Can a minor drive a vehicle?

options.a: Never.
options.b: Yes, as long as an adult who holds a driving licence goes with them.
options.c: No, unless they drive a small-sized vehicle.
options.d: Yes, as long as they are over 16 and have a licence or provisional permit, as set out in the National Regulation of the Driving Licence Issuing System.

explanation: Yes, from 16 — if they have a licence or a provisional permit. An adult passenger does not replace a licence. A small vehicle changes nothing either.
trap: Both b and d start with «Sí, siempre y cuando» (yes, as long as). The right one mentions «16 años» and «permiso provisional» (provisional permit).

b.es: de una personas mayor de edad
y titular de una licencia de conducir.

d.es: y cuente con licencia de conducir

text: It is a general traffic obligation that ____________ move about respecting the messages of _______________, the instructions of Traffic Police officers and the mandate of the relevant laws and regulations.

options.a: Pedestrians - the signboards installed on public roads.
options.b: Road users - traffic control devices.
options.c: Vehicles - the media.
options.d: Minors - senior citizens.

gist: Who must obey what on the road
explanation: The rule applies to all road users: drivers, pedestrians, passengers. They all obey traffic control devices: signs, lights, markings. The other options are too narrow or make no sense.

text.es: Es una obligación general de tránsito
text.tr: It is a general traffic obligation

text.es: de los Efectivos de la Policía de Tránsito
de las normas legales y reglamentarias

b.es: Los usuarios de la vía pública -
los dispositivos de control de tránsito.

text: Mark the incorrect statement:

options.a: It is forbidden to throw, leave or abandon objects on the public road, or any other obstacle that may hinder traffic.
options.b: The driver must keep enough fuel in the vehicle to avoid stopping on the road.
options.c: Vehicles must drive on urban roads with low beams 24 hours a day.
options.d: If there is water on the roadway, the driver must take care not to splash the pavement and pedestrians.

explanation: The question asks for the WRONG statement. Low beams in the city are for night and poor visibility, not 24 hours. Statements a, b and d are real rules.
trap: Look for the false one. The trap is «24 horas del día» (24 hours a day): city low beams are not required all day.

b.es: para evitar detenciones en la vía.
b.tr: to avoid stopping on the road.

text: If, driving along an avenue, you see a sign showing a maximum limit of 50 km/h, but under the rules the maximum speed on that road is 60 km/h; you:

options.a: Must obey the speed sign installed on the road.
options.b: May go at a maximum speed of 60 km/h.
options.c: Must go at a maximum speed of 60 km/h.
options.d: Must go at a speed between 50 and 60 km/h.

explanation: The sign on the road beats the general rule. If the sign says 50, drive at 50 or less. The options with 60 km/h are a trap.

text.es: se encuentra con una señal en la vía
text.tr: you find a sign on the road

text.es: conforme a lo dispuesto en la norma

text: About driving in reverse, mark the correct option:

options.a: It is forbidden, except in strictly justified cases.
options.b: It must never be done.
options.c: It is allowed
options.d: It is allowed, except on highways.

explanation: Reversing is generally forbidden. The only exception is when it is strictly necessary, for example when parking. «Nunca» (never) is too strict, and «permitida» (allowed) is wrong.
trap: Both a and d contain «salvo» (except). The right one says «prohibida» (forbidden) plus «estrictamente justificados» (strictly justified).

text: The use of ___________ beam is mandatory on __________, and you must switch to ____________ beam just before meeting a vehicle coming the other way.

options.a: Low - highways - high.
options.b: High - urban roads - low.
options.c: Fog lights - highways - low.
options.d: High - highways - low.

gist: Which beam is mandatory on highways
explanation: On highways, high beam is mandatory. Before an oncoming car, switch to low beam so you do not dazzle. In the city, high beam is not used.
trap: Word order: «Alta» (high) → «carreteras» (highways) → «baja» (low). Option a is reversed, b says «vías urbanas» (city). Option d has a typo «carretereras».

text: Indicate the permitted behaviour:

options.a: Parking a vehicle at the exit of entertainment venues that are open.
options.b: Parking an emergency vehicle in a place where it is not allowed, if absolutely necessary.
options.c: Parking a vehicle 1 metre past a pedestrian crossing.
options.d: Parking a vehicle on the pavement.

explanation: Ambulances, fire trucks and police may stop anywhere if it is absolutely necessary. Theatre exits, right next to a crossing, and pavements are all forbidden.
trap: All four start the same: «El estacionamiento de un vehículo». Look for «vehículo de emergencia» (emergency vehicle) and «imprescindible» (absolutely necessary).

text: A vehicle is considered abandoned when:

options.a: The vehicle is parked in a permitted place on the public road, but without a driver for more than 72 hours.
options.b: The vehicle is parked in a permitted place on the public road, but without a driver for more than 96 hours.
options.c: The vehicle is parked in a permitted place on the public road, but without a driver and for more than 48 hours.
options.d: The traffic rules say nothing about vehicle abandonment.

gist: When a vehicle counts as abandoned
explanation: A vehicle left without a driver for more than 48 hours is abandoned. Even if the place is allowed. Remember the number: 48 hours, that is two days.
trap: a, b and c differ only by the number: 72, 96, 48. The right one is «48 horas».

text: When carrying a load in your vehicle, you must:

options.a: Make sure that, if the load sticks out sideways from the body, it is well secured.
options.b: Avoid any risk of the load that sticks out sideways from the body falling.
options.c: Try to keep the load from being dragged.
options.d: Make sure the load does not exceed the dimensions of the body.

explanation: The load must not stick out beyond the body of the vehicle. Options a and b accept a load sticking out sideways, which is forbidden. Option c is too soft: «trying» is not enough.
trap: a and b say «sobresalga lateralmente» (sticks out sideways) — a trap. The right one says «no sobrepase las dimensiones» (does not exceed the dimensions).

a.tr: in case the load sticks out

text: About vehicle emission of polluting substances, mark the correct option:

options.a: It is allowed.
options.b: It is forbidden at a level above the maximum limit that the rules allow.
options.c: It is forbidden in urban areas.
options.d: The rules do not regulate it.

explanation: Every car has exhaust, so it cannot be banned completely. What is forbidden is exceeding the maximum limit set by the rules. The place (city or not) does not matter.

text: The competent authority, ______________ may prohibit or restrict _____________________ on certain public roads.

options.a: When the situation justifies it - vehicle traffic or parking.
options.b: Even when the situation justifies it, not - vehicle traffic or parking.
options.c: Is not empowered nor - vehicle traffic
options.d: Only with the driver's consent - vehicle traffic.

gist: When authorities can close a road
explanation: Authorities can close a road or ban parking when the situation requires it. Examples: roadworks, events, accidents. The driver's consent is not needed. Options b and c say they «cannot», which is wrong.
trap: a and b look alike, but b has «Aun cuando… no» (even when… not), meaning «cannot». The right one is a: «Cuando la situación lo justifique» (when the situation justifies it).

text: If, driving on a highway at night, a vehicle approaches from the opposite direction; you must:

options.a: Switch from low beam to high beam
options.b: Turn on the hazard lights.
options.c: Switch from high beam to low beam.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: Oncoming car at night: which beam
explanation: At night on a highway you drive with high beam. When a car comes towards you, switch to low beam to avoid dazzling. Hazard lights are not for this.
trap: a and c use the same words in a different order. Right: «altas a luces bajas» (from high to low).

text.es: Si al conducir en una carretera

text: Stopping a vehicle must be done:

options.a: Against the direction of traffic and in the left lane of the road.
options.b: In the direction of traffic and in the right lane, using high beam.
options.c: In the direction of traffic and in the left lane, using the hazard lights.
options.d: In the direction of traffic and in the right lane, using the hazard lights.

gist: How to stop on the road correctly
explanation: Stop with the traffic, in the right lane, with hazard lights on. The left lane and high beam are wrong.
trap: You need both: «carril derecho» (right lane) and «luces intermitentes» (hazard lights). b has the right lane but «luces altas»; c has hazard lights but «izquierdo».

b.es: En el sentido de la circulación

c.es: En el sentido de la circulación

d.es: En el sentido de la circulación

text: In a traffic accident with injuries and/or material damage, those involved must:

options.a: Go to the fire station.
options.b: Call a relative.
options.c: Request the intervention of the police.
options.d: Leave the place where the accident happened.

gist: What to do after an accident
explanation: After an accident, those involved must call the police. Leaving the scene is forbidden — it is a serious offence. A relative or the fire station is not what the law requires.

text.es: En caso de un accidente de tránsito
text.tr: In case of a traffic accident

text: Before starting to drive a vehicle, the driver is NOT obliged to:

options.a: Carry the vehicle identification card of the vehicle they drive.
options.b: Carry and display the Single Licence Plate.
options.c: Check that the vehicle has a valid SOAT.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: What a driver is not obliged to
explanation: Trap: the question asks what is «not» required. But all three actions are mandatory: card, plate, SOAT. So the right answer is «none of the options».
trap: Read «no está obligado» (not obliged). a, b, c are real duties, so the answer is d «Ninguna de las alternativas es correcta».

text: It enables and authorizes the vehicle to move on the public road, identifies the property and, therefore, the owner responsible for actions arising from that property.

options.a: Vehicle identification card.
options.b: Provincial municipality.
options.c: The National Superintendency of Customs and Tax Administration - SUNAT.
options.d: Single National Licence Plate.

gist: What authorizes travel and identifies the vehicle
explanation: This describes the licence plate (placa). It authorizes driving on public roads and identifies the vehicle and its owner. The card (tarjeta) proves ownership, but «faculta la circulación» refers to the placa.
trap: The trap is «Tarjeta de identificación vehicular» (a): also a vehicle document. But the definition «La faculta y autoriza la circulación» belongs to the «Placa» (licence plate).

text: To determine the presence of alcohol or narcotic substances in the driver, the Traffic Police officer may demand at the stop:

options.a: That they perform coordination and balance tests.
options.b: Use of the breathalyser.
options.c: Blood alcohol test.
options.d: All the options are correct.

gist: Which alcohol tests police may demand
explanation: The police may demand any of these tests: coordination tests, breathalyser, blood test. All three are legal, so the answer is «all the options».
trap: a, b and c are each correct on their own. When all three are right, pick «Todas las alternativas son correctas» (all options are correct).

text.es: el efectivo de la Policía de Tránsito

text.tr: at the time of the stop:

text: Does the National Traffic Regulation take repeat offences into account?

options.a: No, the driver may commit the same offence several times and the penalty will be the same.
options.b: Yes, if the driver commits the same offence within 12 months, the fine is doubled.
options.c: Only in cases of very serious offences.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

gist: Does the regulation count repeat offences
explanation: Yes, repeat offences exist. The same offence within 12 months means double the fine. This applies to any offence, not only very serious ones.

a.es: y la sanción será la misma.
a.tr: and the penalty will be the same.

b.es: con el doble de la multa.

text: After what time from committing the same offence is it called a repeat offence and punished with double the set fine?

options.a: 6 months.
options.b: 12 months.
options.c: 24 months.
options.d: 35 months.

explanation: The number to remember is 12 months. If the same offence repeats within a year, the fine is doubled. The other numbers are just distractors.
trap: All options are numbers. Remember: reincidencia = «12 meses» (one year).

text.tr: is it called a repeat offence

text.es: con el doble de la multa establecida?

text: If an offending driver's driving licence has been suspended, they are entitled to:

options.a: Apply for a duplicate of their driving licence.
options.b: Apply for the renewal of their driving licence.
options.c: Apply for a category upgrade of their driving licence.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: While the licence is suspended, nothing can be done with it. No duplicate, no renewal, no new category. So the answer is «Ninguna»: none of the options.
trap: Options a–c sound like normal procedures, but with a suspension («suspendieron») all of them are blocked. Look for «Ninguna de las alternativas» (none of the options).

text: The __________ serve to inform road users about the general services near the road, such as telephone, lodging, restaurant, first aid, fuel station, workshops and others.

options.a: Location signs.
options.b: Immediate exit signs.
options.c: General services signs.
options.d: Ordinary signs

explanation: The answer repeats the words from the question: «servicios generales» (general services). These signs show a telephone, lodging, fuel station, workshop. Look for the same words in the option.

text: Is it an offence to apply for a duplicate of a driving licence that has been retained?

options.a: It is not an offence.
options.b: Only when the licence was retained for committing a very serious offence.
options.c: Yes, it is an offence.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: If the licence is retained («retenida»), you cannot get a duplicate. It is an offence in itself, with no exceptions. The correct option starts with «Si» (yes).
trap: Options a and c look alike: «No constituye» (is not) vs «Si, constituye» (yes, it is). Option b with «Solo cuando» (only when) adds a false condition.

text: Road markings on the pavement are ___________ signalling and are used to _____________ traffic.

options.a: Horizontal - to regulate.
options.b: Vertical - to regulate.
options.c: Most important - to improve.
options.d: Least important - to decorate.

explanation: Markings are painted on the road, so they are horizontal. Signs on posts are vertical. Markings regulate traffic, they do not decorate it.
trap: Options a and b differ by one word: «Horizontal» is right, «Vertical» is not.

text: Cyclist is to cycle lane as:

options.a: Driver - sidewalk.
options.b: Driver - roadway.
options.c: Driver - shoulder.
options.d: Pedestrian - motorway.

explanation: A cyclist rides on the cycle lane. A driver drives on the roadway, «calzada». The sidewalk («acera») is for pedestrians, the shoulder («berma») is not for driving.

text: The following sign (P-15) is used to warn the driver of:

options.a: The approach to a three-lane road.
options.b: The approach to a hurricane.
options.c: The approach to a winding road.
options.d: The approach to a roundabout intersection (oval or rotary).

explanation: The sign shows three arrows going in a circle. That is a roundabout: «rotonda» or «óvalo». A yellow diamond means a warning.

a.es: a una vía de tres carriles.

text: The following sign (P-31a) indicates:

options.a: The approach to the end of the road.
options.b: The approach to a paved road.
options.c: The approach to a slight slope.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: The sign shows a road ending at a barrier. It warns that the road ends ahead: «final de la vía». Do not confuse it with paving or a slope.

a.tr: of the end of the road.

text: It is a line across the roadway which tells the driver that they must stop the vehicle completely, without going past the start of that line:

options.a: Lane line.
options.b: Roadway edge line.
options.c: Stop line.
options.d: All the options are correct.

gist: Cross line for a full stop
explanation: «Pare» means «stop». The stop line runs across the road; you must stop fully before it. Lane and edge lines run along the road.

text: Traffic lights are:

options.a: Traffic control devices whose purpose is to regulate and control vehicle traffic, motorised and non-motorised, and pedestrian traffic, through the signals of their lights.
options.b: Traffic control devices whose purpose is to regulate and control only motorised vehicle and pedestrian traffic, through light signals.
options.c: Red, green and yellow signals whose only purpose is to regulate the flow of vehicles.
options.d: Devices that emit coloured lights whose only purpose is to regulate the flow of motor vehicles and pedestrians.

explanation: Traffic lights regulate all traffic: cars, bicycles («no motorizado») and pedestrians. The right option is the fullest one, without «únicamente» (only). Options b, c and d leave something out.
trap: Options a and b start the same. Look for «no motorizado» (non-motorised): only the right one has it. «únicamente» and «único fin» (only) mark wrong options.

text: Driving requires a high level of attention, because there are distractions that can cause traffic accidents, for example:

options.a: Worries.
options.b: Use of a mobile phone.
options.c: Operating the radio while driving.
options.d: All the options are correct.

explanation: Worries, the phone and the radio all take attention off the road. Every option is true, so «Todas» (all) is the answer.
trap: Options a, b and c are all true, so it is tempting to pick one. When all fit, look for «Todas las alternativas» (all the options).

text: Does drowsiness affect the ability to drive?

options.a: Yes, because the driver will make slow decisions that lead to mistakes.
options.b: Yes, because the driver is in a bad mood.
options.c: No, as long as driving is done slowly.
options.d: No, as long as driving is done with a companion.

explanation: A drowsy driver thinks slowly and makes mistakes. So the answer is «Si»: yes, it affects driving. Driving slowly or having a companion does not cancel drowsiness.
trap: Option b also starts with «Si», but the reason is wrong: «mal genio» (bad mood). The right reason is «decisiones lentas» (slow decisions).

b.es: el conductor está de mal genio.
b.tr: the driver is in a bad mood.

text: What is the driver's correct action, according to traffic rules, in the situation shown in the following picture?

options.a: Turn right quickly before the pedestrian crosses the roadway.
options.b: Give way to the pedestrian so they can cross the roadway.
options.c: Turn right slowly before the pedestrian crosses the roadway.
options.d: Sound the horn so the pedestrian does not cross the roadway

explanation: In the picture the car turns right while a pedestrian is crossing. A pedestrian on the crossing always has priority. Stop and let them cross.
trap: Options a, c and d say «antes que el peatón cruce» (before the pedestrian crosses) or use the horn. All of them fail to give way. Only «Dar preferencia de paso» (give way) is right.

d.es: para que el peatón no cruce
d.tr: so the pedestrian does not cross

text: In which of the following options do the listed factors contribute to a vehicle collision?

options.a: Dry pavement, drowsiness, worn brakes.
options.b: Wet pavement, worn tyres, fatigue.
options.c: Speed bumps, lack of attention, use of a mobile phone.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: The right option is the one where all three factors are dangerous. Wet road, worn tyres and fatigue are all dangerous. In a, «pavimento seco» (dry pavement) is safe; in c, speed bumps are safe.
trap: Every option has some dangerous words. Pick the one with nothing safe in it: «húmedo» (wet), «neumáticos desgastados» (worn tyres), «cansancio» (fatigue).

text.tr: In which of the following options,

text: The __________ is the part of a highway or road next to the roadway, not intended for vehicle traffic and used occasionally for emergency stops and pedestrian movement.

options.a: Shoulder.
options.b: Motorway.
options.c: Sidewalk.
options.d: Markings.

gist: Road part next to the roadway
explanation: «Berma» is the shoulder: the strip next to the roadway. No driving there, only emergency stops and pedestrians. «Acera» is the city sidewalk, a different thing.

text: It is the part of the road intended for vehicle traffic and occasionally for pedestrians and animals to cross.

options.a: The roadway.
options.b: The sidewalk.
options.c: The shoulder.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: Vehicles drive on the roadway («calzada»). Pedestrians only cross it. The sidewalk is for pedestrians; the shoulder is not for driving.

text.es: Es una parte de la vía
text.tr: It is a part of the road

text.es: destinada a la circulación de vehículos

text: It is the part of the road intended for use by pedestrians

options.a: The sidewalk.
options.b: The roadway.
options.c: The shoulder.
options.d: The motorway.

explanation: Pedestrians walk on the sidewalk, «acera». The roadway is for cars; the shoulder is for emergency stops. Three words are easy to mix up: acera, calzada, berma.

text.es: Es una parte de la vía
text.tr: It is a part of the road

text: Signals that regulate traffic are:

options.a: Horns and markings on the roadway, or horizontal signs.
options.b: Horns and vertical signs.
options.c: Vertical signs, markings on the roadway (horizontal signs) and horns.
options.d: Vertical signs and markings on the roadway, or horizontal signs.

gist: What regulates traffic: signs and markings
explanation: Traffic is regulated by signs on posts (vertical) and markings (horizontal). The horn is not a regulating signal, just a sound. The right option is the only one without «bocinas».
trap: Three of the four options contain «bocinas» (horns): they are wrong. The right one is «señales verticales y las marcas» without «bocinas».

a.es: y las marcas en la calzada

d.es: y las marcas en la calzada

text: Vehicles must be driven with:

options.a: Doors and bonnet closed; the boot may be ajar in special cases.
options.b: Doors, bonnet and boot closed.
options.c: Doors, bonnet and boot closed, except with special authorisation.
options.d: Bonnet and boot closed; two doors may be ajar in special cases.

explanation: Everything must be closed: doors, bonnet and boot. No exceptions and no «special cases». The right option is the shortest one, with no conditions.
trap: Option c repeats the right one but adds «salvo autorización especial» (except with special authorisation). a and d add «permitiéndose» (allowing). Any exception makes it wrong.

text: A driver who on an urban road is going to turn left, right or make a U-turn must signal with the indicator light at least:

options.a: 2 seconds before the manoeuvre.
options.b: 1 metre before the manoeuvre.
options.c: 20 metres before the manoeuvre.
options.d: 3 metres before the manoeuvre.

explanation: In town («vía urbana») you signal 20 metres before the manoeuvre. On a highway («carretera») it is 30 metres. Remember the pair: town 20, highway 30.
trap: There is a similar question about «carretera» (highway) with 30 metres. Here it is «vía urbana» (town): 20 metres. Seconds are wrong.

text.es: va a girar a la izquierda,

text: If you are driving on a highway and are going to turn left, you must signal with the indicator light at least:

options.a: 2 seconds before the manoeuvre.
options.b: 2 metres before the manoeuvre.
options.c: 30 metres before the manoeuvre.
options.d: 1 metre before the manoeuvre.

explanation: On a highway («carretera») speed is higher, so you signal 30 metres before. In town it is 20 metres. Remember: highway 30, town 20.
trap: Do not confuse with the «vía urbana» (town) question, where it is 20 metres. Here «carretera» (highway) means 30 metres.

text.es: y va girar a la izquierda,
text.tr: and are going to turn left,

text: Does the private licence of Class and Category A-I allow you to ride motorcycles?

options.a: Yes.
options.b: No
options.c: Only in urban areas.
options.d: Only on highways.

explanation: A-I is a licence for cars. Motorcycles need a Class B licence. So the answer is «No»: not anywhere.
trap: Options c and d start with «Únicamente» (only) and sound like a compromise. But there are no exceptions: only «No».

text.es: de la Clase y Categoría A-I,

text: The following picture shows:

options.a: Vertical and horizontal traffic signalling in a school zone.
options.b: Only vertical traffic signalling in a school zone.
options.c: Only horizontal traffic signalling in a school zone.
options.d: None of the options is correct.

explanation: The picture has signs on posts (vertical) and «ZONA ESCOLAR» painted on the road (horizontal). Both are present. Options with «Únicamente» (only) are wrong.

text: The channelising __________ serve to form the channelising islands for motor traffic at a(n) _________.

options.a: Channelising islands - road.
options.b: Lines - intersection.
options.c: Roads - intersection.
options.d: All the options are correct.

gist: Channelising lines form islands at intersections
explanation: Channelising lines («líneas canalizadoras») are painted at an intersection. They form islands that guide the flows of vehicles. First word «Líneas», second «intersección».
trap: Option a repeats words from the question, «islas canalizadoras»: that is the trap. Look for «Líneas» (lines).

text: If while driving at an intersection you find the following road markings (a yellow grid), it means:

options.a: That you cannot stop the vehicle inside the intersection area.
options.b: That emergency works are being carried out in the marked area.
options.c: That you can only stop the vehicle inside the intersection area.
options.d: That it is a pedestrian refuge island.

gist: Yellow grid: do not stop inside
explanation: A yellow grid at an intersection means «do not block the intersection». Enter only if you can get out. Stopping inside is not allowed.
trap: Options a and c look alike: «no puede detener» (cannot stop) vs «únicamente puede detener» (can only stop). The right one is «no puede».

text.es: las siguientes marcas en el pavimento

b.tr: That there are being carried out

text: According to the following picture, it is correct to say that:

options.a: The overtaking zone starts with the solid yellow lines.
options.b: Drivers may park where the solid lines begin.
options.c: The no-overtaking zone starts with the solid yellow lines.
options.d: The truck driver may park before the solid lines begin

explanation: In the picture the broken yellow line becomes a solid one. You cannot cross a solid yellow line, so overtaking is prohibited. Parking has nothing to do with it.
trap: Options a and c differ by one phrase: «permite adelantar» (allows overtaking) vs «no adelantar» (no overtaking). Solid line = «no adelantar».

text.tr: it is correct to state that:

d.es: antes de empezar las líneas continuas
